## Dimorphos’s Orbit After DART’s Impact

Before DART’s impact, Dimorphos took 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit the larger asteroid Didymos. Immediately afterward, its orbital period was 11 hours, 22 minutes and 37 seconds—a decrease of 32 minutes and 42 seconds.

The change continued over the following weeks. During that time, Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, while its orbital period continued to shorten. The orbit was also no longer circular after the impact.

The period eventually settled at 11 hours, 22 minutes and 3 seconds, 33 minutes and 15 seconds shorter than before the impact.
